context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud and provides case management for human analysts. It operates within strict regulatory, performance, and budgetary constraints using managed cloud infrastructure.

## Key Elements
* Payment Gateway / Acquirer
* Fraud Analysts
* Card Networks & Tokenization Vault
* Regulatory & Audit Authorities
* Core Banking / Ledger System
* ML Model Training Environment
* Identity Provider (IdP)
* API Ingestion & Routing Container
* Real-Time Scoring Engine Container
* Case Management Backend Container
* Audit & Compliance Worker
* Fail-Open Circuit Breaker Proxy
* Model & Rule Sync Service
* Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)
* Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
* Amazon S3 Object Lock

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway to API Ingestion: Synchronous gRPC over TLS 1.3
* Fraud Analysts to Case Management Backend: HTTPS over TLS 1.3 via AWS Client VPN or IAM-authenticated Web UI
* Real-Time Scoring Engine to Amazon ElastiCache: Redis TCP protocol over TLS
* Audit & Compliance Worker to Amazon S3 Object Lock: Asynchronous event export via AWS SDK
* Real-Time Scoring Engine to Audit SQS: AWS SDK async event dispatch

## Technology Stack
* AWS ECS on Fargate: Runs core stateless containers within the 25k EUR budget and 3-engineer constraint
* Go or Rust: High-performance runtime for the Real-Time Scoring Engine to meet <50ms P99 latency
* Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): In-memory cache for sub-millisecond feature lookups and zero-downtime model hot-swapping
* Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Relational database for persistent case management workflows
* Amazon S3 Object Lock: WORM storage ensuring tamper-evident 7-year audit log retention
* Envoy: Circuit breaker proxy ensuring automated fail-open availability under high latency

## Rationale
This architecture uses managed AWS services to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team while respecting a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. High-performance containers and caching guarantee sub-50ms P99 latency and high availability to satisfy strict payment processing SLAs.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
- Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluating card-not-present payment authorizations for mid-size payment processors while supporting manual analyst reviews.
- Designed to meet sub-50ms latency, strict PCI-DSS compliance, and 7-year tamper-evident auditability constraints within a fixed AWS infrastructure budget.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer
- Fraud Analyst UI (React SPA via Amazon S3 / CloudFront)
- API Gateway & Ingress (Java / Spring Cloud Gateway)
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Java / Spring Boot + ONNX)
- Case Management Backend (Node.js / TypeScript)
- Model & Rule Management Service (Python / FastAPI)
- Audit Worker (Node.js / Python worker)
- Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (Scoring DB / Audit Log)
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway to API Gateway & Ingress via HTTPS (REST/gRPC)
- Fraud Analyst to Fraud Analyst UI via HTTPS
- Fraud Analyst UI to Case Management Backend via HTTPS
- API Gateway & Ingress to Real-Time Scoring Engine via gRPC over HTTP/2
- Real-Time Scoring Engine to Amazon ElastiCache via RESP over TCP
- Real-Time Scoring Engine to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams via HTTPS (AWS SDK)
- Audit Worker to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL via TLS/TCP
- Case Management Backend to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL via TLS/TCP
- Model & Rule Management Service to Real-Time Scoring Engine via internal REST API over HTTPS

## Technology Stack
- Java / Spring Cloud Gateway: Handles secure public ingress and enforces PCI-DSS boundaries
- Java / Spring Boot + ONNX: Provides sub-50ms P99 latency scoring with embedded machine learning models
- Node.js / TypeScript: Powers lightweight case management backend workflows
- Python / FastAPI: Manages zero-downtime model and rule updates
- Amazon Kinesis Data Streams: Decouples scoring latency from durable audit logging
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Provides tamper-evident append-only storage for 7-year audit requirements
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Delivers microsecond-latency feature lookups
- React & Amazon S3/CloudFront: Hosts secure single-page analyst interface

## Rationale
- Container decomposition and technology choices align with the skills of a 3-engineer team while respecting the 25,000 EUR monthly AWS budget constraint in `eu-west-1`.
- Asynchronous Kinesis streaming and in-memory model hot-swapping guarantee high performance (<50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS) without compromising strict PCI-DSS and auditability mandates.

Fraud Analyst UI.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations to prevent fraud and provides a review interface for suspicious transactions. It ensures sub-50ms latency, strict PCI-DSS compliance, and 7-year auditability on AWS within a fixed budget.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts: Primary users reviewing suspicious transactions.
- Fraud Analyst UI: React SPA hosted via Amazon S3 and Amazon CloudFront.
- API Gateway & Ingress: Java / Spring Cloud Gateway managing incoming traffic.
- Real-Time Scoring Engine: Java / Spring Boot + ONNX service scoring transactions.
- Case Management Backend: Node.js / TypeScript service managing analyst workflows.
- Model & Rule Management Service: Python / FastAPI service for zero-downtime updates.
- Audit Worker & Supporting Datastores: Node.js/Python workers, Amazon Kinesis, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, and Amazon ElastiCache (Redis).

## Relationships
- Fraud Analysts -> Fraud Analyst UI: Accesses case management workflows and web UI [HTTPS]
- Fraud Analyst UI -> Case Management Backend: Fetches cases and submits review decisions [HTTPS / JSON REST]
- Fraud Analyst UI -> Model & Rule Management Service: Sends rule update payloads [HTTPS / JSON REST]
- Fraud Analyst UI -> API Gateway & Ingress: Transmits secured requests and audit telemetry [HTTPS / JSON REST]

## Technology Stack
- Frontend: React SPA, Zustand, Tailwind CSS, TanStack Table, Axios (hosted on Amazon S3 / CloudFront) for a lightweight, serverless UI.
- Backend Services: Java / Spring Boot, Node.js / TypeScript, and Python / FastAPI to balance high performance and rapid development.
- Data & Streaming: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon ElastiCache (Redis), and Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for reliable persistence, caching, and event streaming.
- Cloud Platform: AWS (eu-west-1 region) to leverage managed services within the fixed budget.

## Rationale
This serverless and managed container architecture minimizes operational overhead for a three-engineer team while easily meeting peak performance and strict PCI-DSS Level 1 security requirements. AWS managed services ensure high availability and robust audit trails within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

Real-Time Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to detect fraud and manage analyst reviews. It ensures sub-50ms P99 latency while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability.

## Key Elements
- Scoring API Controller (`Java / Spring MVC`)
- Feature Aggregator (`Java / Spring Data`)
- Inference Engine (`Java + ONNX Runtime`)
- Decision Evaluator
- Model Hot-Swapper (`Java`)
- Audit Event Publisher (`Java / AWS SDK`)
- Circuit Breaker & Fallback Handler (`Resilience4j`)
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)
- Amazon Kinesis Data Streams

## Relationships
- API Gateway & Ingress -> Scoring API Controller: Ingests requests [gRPC over HTTP/2]
- Scoring API Controller -> Feature Aggregator: Fetches features [Direct Method Call]
- Feature Aggregator -> Amazon ElastiCache: Fetches user velocity profiles [RESP over TCP]
- Scoring API Controller -> Inference Engine: Invokes model inference [In-memory ONNX Runtime API]
- Inference Engine -> Decision Evaluator: Passes raw scores [Direct Method Call]
- Model & Rule Management Service -> Model Hot-Swapper: Pushes model binaries [gRPC / HTTPS]
- Model Hot-Swapper -> Inference Engine: Updates model reference [In-memory pointer swap]
- Decision Evaluator -> Audit Event Publisher: Enqueues logs [ConcurrentQueue]
- Audit Event Publisher -> Amazon Kinesis Data Streams: Publishes batched events [AWS SDK over HTTPS]
- Circuit Breaker & Fallback Handler -> Scoring API Controller: Wraps execution [AOP Interceptor]

## Technology Stack
- Java / Spring Boot: Core container framework matching the engineering team's expertise.
- ONNX Runtime: Executes machine learning models in-process via JNI for ultra-low latency.
- Resilience4j: Enforces circuit breaking and fallbacks to prevent upstream payment blocking.
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Provides high-performance sub-10ms feature lookups.
- Amazon Kinesis Data Streams: Handles asynchronous, tamper-evident audit logging.

## Rationale
This architecture uses in-process ML inference and non-indirection caching to achieve sub-50ms latency without expensive remote scoring hardware. It respects the 3-person team limit and €25k monthly budget while meeting strict auditability and availability mandates.

Case Management Backend.analysis:
## Overview
This architecture defines a real-time payment fraud screening system for card-not-payments, processing 3,000 authorizations per second while enabling fraud analyst case reviews. It enforces PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, maintains 7-year tamper-evident audit logs, and operates within a 25,000 EUR monthly AWS budget managed by three engineers.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst UI (React SPA via Amazon S3 / CloudFront)
- Case Management Backend (Node.js / TypeScript)
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Java / Spring Boot + ONNX)
- Case API Controller (Express.js / TypeScript)
- Case Workflow Service (TypeScript)
- Data Access Repository (Prisma ORM / TypeScript)
- Audit Logging Interceptor (TypeScript)
- Tokenization Gateway Client (Axios / TypeScript)
- Scoring API Controller (Spring WebFlux / Java)
- Feature Assembler (Java)
- Inference Executor (ONNX Runtime via JNI)
- Resilience & Fallback Handler (Resilience4j / Java)
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)

## Relationships
- Fraud Analyst UI -> Case API Controller: Performs case reviews and workflow actions [HTTPS]
- Case API Controller -> Case Workflow Service: Invokes business logic [In-memory function calls]
- Case Workflow Service -> Audit Logging Interceptor: Dispatches audit events [Async/Sync method calls]
- Case Workflow Service -> Data Access Repository: Persists state changes [TypeScript/Prisma]
- Case Workflow Service -> Tokenization Gateway Client: Requests tokenized payload [HTTPS/REST]
- Data Access Repository -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Executes parameterized queries with optimistic locking [TLS/TCP]
- Scoring API Controller -> Resilience4j Fallback Handler: Wraps pipeline execution [In-memory]
- Feature Assembler -> Amazon ElastiCache: Fetches real-time profiles [TCP/Redis Protocol]
- Inference Executor -> ONNX Runtime: Executes fraud model [In-memory via JNI]

## Technology Stack
- AWS (eu-west-1): Provides a scalable cloud infrastructure within the fixed 25,000 EUR budget.
- Node.js & TypeScript: Powers the Case Management Backend for rapid development by a 3-engineer team.
- Java, Spring Boot, & Spring WebFlux: Delivers high-throughput, non-blocking I/O for sub-50ms P99 scoring latency.
- ONNX Runtime via JNI: Eliminates network serialization overhead for in-memory model execution.
- Resilience4j: Implements circuit breakers and fallbacks to satisfy the 1-minute availability constraint.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL & Prisma ORM: Ensures type-safe data access and encrypted, auditable storage.

## Rationale
The architecture combines Node.js for maintainable case management workflows with Java and Spring WebFlux to meet stringent performance requirements. By leveraging in-memory ONNX execution and robust fallback mechanisms, it achieves high availability and low latency within the team and budget constraints.

Model & Rule Management Service.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations and manages case reviews for analysts. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, sub-50ms decision latency, and 7-year tamper-evident auditability within a fixed infrastructure budget.

## Key Elements
- **API Controller**: FastAPI endpoints handling administrative requests over HTTPS.
- **Rule & Model Validator**: Validates rule syntax and ONNX model compatibility.
- **Sandbox Evaluator**: Tests models against historical regression fixtures.
- **Version Registry**: Manages semantic versioning and metadata backed by Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.
- **Artifact Bundler**: Packages models, configurations, and rules into immutable archives.
- **Distribution Publisher**: Publishes rule sets and ONNX binaries via Amazon S3 and Amazon SNS.
- **Audit Event Emitter**: Emits cryptographically signed audit logs via Amazon SQS.

## Relationships
- API Controller -> Rule & Model Validator [In-memory function call]
- Rule & Model Validator -> Version Registry [SQL/ORM over TLS]
- Rule & Model Validator -> Sandbox Evaluator [In-memory function call]
- Sandbox Evaluator -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL [Read historical test fixtures via SQL/ORM over TLS]
- Sandbox Evaluator -> Artifact Bundler [In-memory function call]
- Artifact Bundler -> Distribution Publisher [In-memory function call]
- Distribution Publisher -> Real-Time Scoring Engine [AWS SNS / HTTPS webhook]
- API Controller & Version Registry -> Audit Event Emitter [Internal Event bus]
- Audit Event Emitter -> Audit Worker [Amazon SQS over TLS]

## Technology Stack
- **Python / FastAPI**: Chosen for native Pydantic validation and ONNX runtime ecosystem support.
- **Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL**: Provides robust relational storage for version metadata and test fixtures.
- **Amazon S3 & SNS**: Enables decoupled, reliable distribution of model bundles and atomic hot-reloading.
- **Amazon SQS**: Securely queues tamper-evident audit logs for downstream processing.

## Rationale
This architecture enables zero-downtime model updates and strict audit trails while keeping maintenance overhead minimal for a three-person team. The design ensures cost-efficiency within the 25,000 EUR monthly AWS budget in eu-west-1.

Audit Worker.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to detect fraud and manage analyst reviews. It ensures high performance, PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, and 7-year tamper-evident auditability on AWS.

## Key Elements
- **Audit Event Consumer**: Python (`boto3`) component polling streaming events.
- **Stream Offset Manager**: Python / AWS SDK tracking Kinesis shard iterator positions.
- **Tamper-Evident Signer**: Python (`cryptography`) component generating cryptographic hashes.
- **KMS Integration Wrapper**: Python (`boto3`) interface for AWS KMS envelope encryption.
- **Audit Persistence Adapter**: Python (`psycopg2`) component for database writes.
- **Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) Handler**: Python component capturing failed payloads.

## Relationships
- Audit Event Consumer -> Amazon Kinesis Data Streams: Polls and commits stream offsets [HTTPS]
- Audit Event Consumer -> Tamper-Evident Signer: Passes raw audit payload [In-memory]
- Audit Event Consumer -> Amazon SQS (DLQ): Forwards failed audit events [HTTPS]
- Tamper-Evident Signer -> AWS KMS: Requests signing keys/operations [HTTPS/TLS]
- Tamper-Evident Signer -> Audit Persistence Adapter: Passes signed record [In-memory]
- Audit Persistence Adapter -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Inserts audit log [TLS/TCP]

## Technology Stack
- **Python**: Chosen for rapid implementation by a three-engineer team.
- **`boto3` / AWS SDK**: Integrates natively with AWS services (Kinesis, SQS, KMS).
- **AWS KMS**: Secures signing keys via hardware isolation for PCI-DSS compliance.
- **Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL**: Provides durable, compliant storage for audit records.

## Rationale
This architecture decouples durable logging from real-time scoring to maintain P99 latency below 50 ms. It ensures tamper-evident auditability and PCI-DSS compliance within budget constraints.

- **Enhanced Fan-Out Consumer Endpoints** -> **Audit Worker**: Delivers push-based event streams [HTTP/2 (KCL)]

## Technology Stack
- **Amazon Kinesis Data Streams**: Fully managed streaming service chosen to handle 3,000 TPS with zero infrastructure overhead.
- **AWS Kinesis Client Library (KCL)**: Consumes event streams reliably via HTTP/2 for downstream auditing.
- **AWS Internal Protocols**: Utilized for secure, low-latency cross-component communication within the AWS cloud.

## Rationale
The managed streaming architecture meets high-throughput and low-latency performance targets without exceeding the 3-engineer operational capacity. It satisfies PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability constraints through serverless AWS primitives.

## Overview
The system provides real-time fraud screening for card-not-present payment authorizations and case management for fraud analysts. It screens transactions with sub-50ms latency while ensuring PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst UI (React SPA via Amazon S3 / CloudFront)
- API Gateway & Ingress (Java / Spring Cloud Gateway)
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Java / Spring Boot + ONNX)
- Case Management Backend (Node.js / TypeScript)
- Model & Rule Management Service (Python / FastAPI)
- Audit Worker (Node.js / Python worker)
- Amazon Kinesis Data Streams (Amazon Kinesis)
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL)
- Amazon ElastiCache (Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)):
  - Feature Store Cache (Redis Cluster)
  - Blacklist / Denylist Registry (Redis In-Memory Set / Hash)
  - Session & Idempotency Store (Redis Strings with TTL)
  - Real-Time Model Feature Cache (Redis Sorted Sets)
  - Tokenized Entity Cache (Redis Encrypted Hash)

## Relationships
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Feature Store Cache: Fetches sliding-window user velocity metrics via `RESP` over TCP
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Blacklist Registry: Fast membership checks via `RESP` over TCP
- API Gateway & Ingress -> Session & Idempotency Store: Validates request tokens and locks via `RESP` over TCP
- Audit Worker / Model Service -> Feature Cache: Updates real-time aggregations via `RESP` over TCP
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Tokenized Entity Cache: Fetches token mappings via `RESP over TLS`

## Technology Stack
- AWS (eu-west-1): Target cloud infrastructure provider
- Redis Cluster / ElastiCache: Delivers microsecond-latency feature lookups and sliding-window velocity tracking within budget
- Java / Spring Boot & ONNX: Powers high-throughput, low-latency payment scoring
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Stores auditable transaction decisions and case data

## Rationale
This architecture uses managed AWS services and in-memory caching to achieve sub-50ms latency at 3,000 TPS within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. It enforces PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability while remaining maintainable by a three-engineer team.
